newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A shares close down, B shares inch lower.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares close down, B shares inch lower.

text.p: Shenzhen's A share index closed sharply down on Friday, continuing its nosedive in the previous few days on Beijing's crackdown on the stock markets, with investors turning growingly pessimistic, brokers said.
But the B share index fell only slightly, thanks to cautious demand for stocks with solid earnings records, brokers said.

The A share index plunged 28.89 points or 8.07 percent to 328.96 on turnover of 4.27 billion yuan compared with 7.33 billion yuan for the previous session. The B index edged down 0.98 points or 0.78 percent to 125.56 on volume of 45.80 million shares worth HK$191.59 million against HK$472.61 million.
Brokers said the A share market plunge was also linked to rumours that Beijing is drafting new anti-speculation measures.
"The A index is likely to continue to fall sharply in the coming sessions as confidence had been destroyed by steep falls this week," a broker with China Guotai Securities said.
Investors have scrambled to dump "rubbish stocks", shares in small firms with poor earnings records, the broker said.
Most such shares closed at the 10 percent limit-down level on Friday after their prices had been pushed to high levels by institutional punters in a bull run from April to early this month.

"The inflow of fresh money into A shares had been cut off by the People's Daily conmentary published on Monday," a trader said. "Many domestic investors are disappointed at seeing their share prices diving nearly every day," he added.
Many A shares, mainly cheap and small issues, have fallen by nearly 50 percent in the past seven sessions.
On the B share market, conglomerate Zhonghao was the worst performer, divnng HK$0.42, or 9.93 percent, to HK$3.81 on volume of 260,900 shares.
Tellus Machinery plunged HK$0.30, or 9.84 percent, to HK$2.75 on trade of 830,600 shares.
Changan traded the most on volume of 9.49 million shares and put on HK$0.20 to HK$3.75 due to institutional support, brokers said.
China Marine Container rose HK$0.27, or 3.55 percent, to HK$7.88 after 186,800 shares changed hands. The company had solid earnings in the past two years.
